title: Gender dynamics: mechanisms and open questions
scope: Two supplied analytical briefs; 40 proposed mechanisms. This is not an analysis of verified original recordings.

sources.title: Implicit expectations and relational conflict
sources.type: User-supplied analytical brief about an unavailable podcast
sources.limitations: The brief describes an autistic speaker and an incomplete recording excerpt. That context is retained; extension to other people is a hypothesis, not evidence of prevalence.
sources.summary: Proposes that implicit expectations, missed cues and negative motive attribution can turn misunderstandings into conflict and exclusion.

sources.title: Moral judgment, accountability and gendered trust
sources.type: User-supplied analytical brief about an unavailable podcast
sources.limitations: Case descriptions, alleged reactions and legal/medical claims have not been independently verified.
sources.summary: Proposes a path from morally salient events through perceived group favoritism to wider distrust and polarization.

mechanisms.name: Invisible relational contracts
mechanisms.claim: Unspoken expectations for affirmation, attention and loyalty may be interpreted as agreements.
mechanisms.alternative: A missed response may reflect a different convention rather than rejection.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare explicitly negotiated and implicit expectations across relationships.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Covert reciprocity
mechanisms.claim: Care or compliments may carry an unstated expectation of repayment; a literal thank-you can then be interpreted as insufficient.
mechanisms.alternative: The gesture may be generous without any repayment expectation.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Ask both participants what they intended and expected before coding social debt.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Delayed rupture
mechanisms.claim: Unspoken grievances may accumulate while outward friendliness continues, making a later break seem sudden.
mechanisms.alternative: A relationship can change for reasons unrelated to accumulated resentment.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Collect repeated reports from both partners rather than infer private feelings from one account.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: You should have known
mechanisms.claim: A person may expect needs or offenses to be inferred without an explicit request.
mechanisms.alternative: Relevant expectations may previously have been discussed or misunderstood.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Measure expectation clarity, cue access and opportunities for repair separately.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Opaque sanctions
mechanisms.claim: Exclusion without an explanation can leave the recipient unable to identify or correct the alleged violation.
mechanisms.alternative: Withdrawal may be a boundary rather than punishment, and its cause may be unrelated.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Document the actual feedback, timing and each participant’s account.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding

sourceLocation.heading: THEORY 5: RELATIONAL SANCTION WITHOUT PROCEDURAL WARNING

mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Relational hypervigilance
mechanisms.claim: Repeated unexpected rejection is proposed to encourage retrospective analysis and excessive monitoring of future interactions.
mechanisms.alternative: Prior anxiety, stress or other experiences could explain monitoring.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Use longitudinal evidence before attributing monitoring to these encounters.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Identity coordination
mechanisms.claim: Differences in interests or appearance may be read as threats to similarity and belonging.
mechanisms.alternative: Shared rituals may be voluntary and affirming rather than coercive.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare autonomy, consent and reactions to difference across contexts.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Externalized self-evaluation
mechanisms.claim: One person’s activity may trigger another’s self-comparison and a demand for reassurance.
mechanisms.alternative: A self-comparing remark may be conversation rather than a request for emotional labor.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Distinguish expressed insecurity from an actual demand for reassurance.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding

sourceLocation.heading: THEORY 8: SOCIAL COMPARISON AS INTERPERSONAL REGULATION

mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Relational power
mechanisms.claim: The brief proposes that alliances, reputation and inclusion can function as informal resources of influence.
mechanisms.alternative: Formal power, culture and organizational structure may better explain an episode.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: The proposed historical gender explanation needs independent comparative research.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding

sourceLocation.heading: THEORY 9: RELATIONAL POWER AND NETWORK SANCTIONS

mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Ritual and intention
mechanisms.claim: Failure to mirror, affirm or participate in a ritual may be interpreted as unwillingness instead of a missed cue.
mechanisms.alternative: A person can knowingly decline a ritual without hostile intent.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare observers’ attributions with participants’ reported intentions.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding

sourceLocation.heading: THEORY 10: SOCIAL-RITUAL COMPETENCE AS GROUP MEMBERSHIP SIGNAL

mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Social-competence expectation mismatch
mechanisms.claim: The source proposes that perceived attractiveness can raise expected social competence and intensify negative motive attribution.
mechanisms.alternative: Attractiveness may have different or no effects in other settings.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Test the proposed moderator; neither its direction nor size is established here.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Intentionality inflation
mechanisms.claim: Silence, awkwardness or independence may be assigned a strategic or hostile motive.
mechanisms.alternative: Intentional behavior is also possible; interpretation alone establishes neither motive.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare fatigue, preference, communication difference and intentional explanations.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Outsider cascade
mechanisms.claim: A negative interpretation may circulate through a network and consolidate into exclusion.
mechanisms.alternative: Others may reach independent judgments or dispute the original account.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Trace who learned what from whom; do not assume consensus or contagion.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Asymmetric error costs
mechanisms.claim: Someone who expects severe consequences for missed cues may over-monitor even harmless signals.
mechanisms.alternative: Perceived risk can differ from actual consequences.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Separate expected costs, observed sanctions and false alarms.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Autonomy-safe relationships
mechanisms.claim: The brief proposes direct requests, tolerated differences and repair as conditions for safer relationships.
mechanisms.alternative: Explicit communication can also be coercive; directness alone is insufficient.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare consent, autonomy and repair outcomes instead of assuming a universal ideal.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding

sourceLocation.heading: THEORY 15: RELATIONAL SAFETY AS AUTONOMY WITHOUT PENALTY

mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Moral shock
mechanisms.claim: A salient event may activate old grievances and reorganize a person’s interpretation of earlier events.
mechanisms.alternative: A reported shift may be temporary or reflect pre-existing views.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Measure attitudes before and after exposure with a comparison group.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Identity-protective accountability
mechanisms.claim: Identification with an accused person may motivate more attention to mitigating explanations.
mechanisms.alternative: Evidence, clinical beliefs or legal standards may explain contextualization without group loyalty.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Separate identity, evidence evaluation, empathy and culpability judgments.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: In-group exoneration
mechanisms.claim: The brief proposes more situational explanations for an in-group actor than for an out-group actor.
mechanisms.alternative: Similar defenses may occur across sexes and other identities.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Use matched scenarios varying actor identity while holding relevant facts constant.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Accountability displacement
mechanisms.claim: Unsupported alternative narratives may preserve a favored group’s image when an allegation threatens it.
mechanisms.alternative: An alternative account can be justified if supported by evidence.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Check each allegation independently; do not infer conspiracy from discussion of coercion or illness.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Empathy and accountability
mechanisms.claim: Compassion and responsibility are separate judgments, even when a debate frames them as competing.
mechanisms.alternative: Empathy for one person need not exclude empathy for victims.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Code compassion, mitigation and exoneration independently.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Paternalistic boomerang
mechanisms.claim: An argument for reduced responsibility may be generalized by observers into a claim of reduced group competence.
mechanisms.alternative: Observers may keep a specific impairment separate from general capability.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Test audience interpretations; no demographic incapacity follows from a particular case.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Agency and responsibility
mechanisms.claim: The brief links perceived control over an act with attributed responsibility.
mechanisms.alternative: Different moral and legal frameworks can weigh control differently.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Distinguish causal explanation, moral judgment and legal standards.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Institutional trust spillover
mechanisms.claim: A disputed judgment may be generalized from an individual decision-maker to an institution.
mechanisms.alternative: Trust may change because of procedures or evidence rather than demographic identity.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Measure case-specific and institutional trust separately.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Civic competence inference
mechanisms.claim: Judgments in one domain may be used to question an entire group’s civic competence.
mechanisms.alternative: Domain-specific disagreement does not establish a stable group trait.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Analyze the inference without endorsing restrictions on civic participation.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Parallel moral frames
mechanisms.claim: Observers may emphasize victims, suffering, intent, responsibility or fairness differently.
mechanisms.alternative: Individuals can hold several priorities simultaneously; these are not fixed male/female camps.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Measure moral priorities rather than assign a framework by sex.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Identity-shaped evidence selection
mechanisms.claim: Group identity may shape which accounts feel credible and which explanations receive attention.
mechanisms.alternative: Expertise, information access and evidence quality can also explain disagreement.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare source exposure and evidence weighting across identities.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Role-based moral legitimacy
mechanisms.claim: The brief proposes that association with a valued role can confer moral authority.
mechanisms.alternative: Role expectations and authority vary across societies and individuals.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Historical claims about motherhood and moral authority need separate evidence.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Sacred-role violation
mechanisms.claim: An act perceived as violating a valued role may provoke particularly intense moral shock.
mechanisms.alternative: The harm itself may explain the reaction without a role-based mechanism.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare equally harmful acts while varying role expectations.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Symbolic representative error
mechanisms.claim: A highly visible subset may be treated as representative of an entire demographic group.
mechanisms.alternative: An observer may accurately distinguish the subset from the wider population.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare perceived prevalence with representative evidence.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Availability cascade
mechanisms.claim: Repeated exposure to extreme examples may increase perceived frequency and fuel further engagement.
mechanisms.alternative: A real change in prevalence could also contribute.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Separate repeated exposure, unique examples and population rates.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Accumulated grievance
mechanisms.claim: A new event may become a last straw that consolidates earlier grievances.
mechanisms.alternative: The apparent threshold may be a retrospective narrative rather than a distinct change.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Track prior attitudes and competing explanations over time.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Cross-domain belief cascade
mechanisms.claim: An interpretation of one event may spread to beliefs about relationships, parenthood and institutions.
mechanisms.alternative: Views across domains may have shared prior causes.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Test whether exposure predicts change beyond baseline ideology.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Relationship moral sorting
mechanisms.claim: Discussion of a third-party event may reveal differences in values and trigger trust reassessment.
mechanisms.alternative: The discussion may expose rather than create an existing incompatibility.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Distinguish discovery of disagreement from subsequent relationship effects.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Moral projection correction
mechanisms.claim: An idealized view of a partner may be revised after a moral disagreement.
mechanisms.alternative: The revised negative view can be as stereotyped as the original idealization.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Assess the individual partner rather than infer virtue from identity.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Trust revision
mechanisms.claim: Observers may update expectations of fairness, care or reliability after salient examples.
mechanisms.alternative: A belief update can be biased and need not improve accuracy.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Record both the update and whether its evidence supports its scope.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Backlash loop
mechanisms.claim: Perceived favoritism may produce distrust; defensive solidarity may then be taken as confirmation.
mechanisms.alternative: Defensiveness may respond to real hostility rather than confirm the original allegation.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Trace both directions and consider interventions that interrupt escalation.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Postpartum stigma boomerang
mechanisms.claim: The brief predicts that extreme-case associations could discourage disclosure through fear and scrutiny.
mechanisms.alternative: Clinical education or supportive discussion could instead reduce stigma and improve disclosure.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: This is an untested communication hypothesis, not a clinical claim about postpartum people.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Advocacy backfire
mechanisms.claim: A message intended to build compassion may be interpreted as a signal of threat or reduced responsibility.
mechanisms.alternative: Advocacy may also improve understanding and support.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Compare message framing and audience responses without assuming a negative effect.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Perceived accountability asymmetry
mechanisms.claim: Different reactions to apparently comparable actors may be perceived as a moral double standard.
mechanisms.alternative: The cases may differ in relevant facts, evidence or legal context.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Use genuinely matched cases and separate perception from demonstrated unequal treatment.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

mechanisms.name: Moral delegitimation
mechanisms.claim: Disagreement with visible individuals may lead to discounting future claims from their whole group.
mechanisms.alternative: An observer may reject a specific argument without rejecting its demographic source.
mechanisms.researchNeeded: Test identity-based credibility judgments while holding argument content constant.
mechanisms.evidenceStatus: Source-derived hypothesis; not an externally verified finding
mechanisms.verificationStatus: Primary source and comparative empirical evidence pending

verificationQueue.needed: Recording URLs, speaker identities, dates and the actual transcript excerpts; resolve the non-functional citation placeholders.
Representative comparative research before claims about most women, most men or sex-specific prevalence.
Primary legal records for procedural history, verdict or trial claims, jury statements and allegations involving other people. None is established here.
Authoritative clinical sources before any factual statement about diagnosis, prevalence, risk or treatment; do not generalize from a criminal case.
Comparable cohorts and confounder controls for parent gender, custody, parental alienation and child outcomes.
Sampling methods and longitudinal measures of opinion, trust, relationships and stigma; visible posts are not representative surveys.

codingRule: Proposed constructs are organizational labels from the supplied briefs, not validated scales or established named theories. Null means not measured, never zero.
